title: Google AI Pro subscription
badge: Price verified on official subscriptions page
catchSummary: The $19.99 fee bundles a lot (5 TB storage, 4x Gemini usage, apps) but the AI limits are window-shaped — a 5-hour refresh that stops at a weekly ceiling — and the annual price is never shown on official pages.

official_links.label: Google AI subscription plans (official)
official_links.note: Read live 2026-09-07 — the only fetched official page whose static text carries the dollar price ($19.99/mo), the 5-hour/weekly limit mechanism, and the no-partial-refund line.

price.now: $19.99/mo (annual billing is offered but the annual price is not published on official pages fetched)
price.renewal: Auto-renews at the start of each billing cycle until you unsubscribe; price increases require at least 30 days' prior notice applied after the current period; a failed renewal gets a seven-day grace period.

renewal: Charged at the beginning of each billing cycle; renews automatically unless canceled. Google may change prices with at least 30 days' notice before your next charge. Cancellations keep benefits until the cycle ends; storage purchases are non-refundable in most countries (Apple-billed purchases go through Apple; Israel has a 14-day pro-rata rule).
eligibility: Available in over 150 countries and territories; personal Google accounts only (not while billed via a third-party partner or Pixel Pass)
Students: Google AI Pro free for 1 year with SheerID verification — offer auto-renews at $19.99/mo when student status concludes; not available on school-issued accounts
Family sharing: up to five other members get AI benefits at no extra cost (with carve-outs, e.g. YouTube Premium Lite not shareable)
restrictions: Limits are per-window: 'Your limit refreshes every 5 hours until you reach your weekly limit' — and each product (Gemini, Flow, Antigravity…) has its own limits
Exact prompts/day or gens/week figures: not published on fetched official pages
Buying more usage exists (AI credits) but pack prices and per-feature credit costs are not published in the help article and 'Google reserves the right to modify the credit cost'
Feature flags are region-limited: auto-browse in Chrome and Photos Remix are US-only per the plans page
The one.google.com plans pages render prices client-side — dollar figures were confirmed only on gemini.google/subscriptions
verdict: Google AI Pro is less an AI subscription than a bundle: $19.99/mo buys 5 TB of storage, roughly 4x Gemini usage vs non-subscribers, Gemini across Gmail/Docs, Flow, NotebookLM, Jules, Antigravity, Home Premium, and $10/mo of Cloud credits. For anyone already inside Google Workspace for personal life, it is the best value-per-dollar of the $20 class even if you rarely prompt. For AI-first power users the ceiling is real: a weekly cap over each product, no published numbers, and a credits top-up whose price you discover at checkout. Students get a free year — that alone flips the comparison for eligible users.
catches: The weekly limit sits above the 5-hour window: bursty days are survivable, sustained weeks are the actual ceiling
Annual billing exists but its price is never shown on official pages fetched this pass — you discover it at checkout
AI-credit packs: mechanism official, pricing unpublished, and per-feature costs are stated to be modifiable by Google
Cancel means you keep AI until cycle end, then storage drops to the 15 GB free tier — if your data lives on the 5 TB, downgrading is a migration project
limits: Usage vs free tier: '4x access to Gemini' (footnoted 'in comparison to non-AI subscribers'); higher caps for Gemini 3.1 Pro, Deep Research, 1M-token context, ~1,500-page uploads
No published per-day counts for prompts, Deep Research runs, or Flow generations — only the 5-hour-refresh/weekly-limit mechanism
Only the plan manager can purchase AI credits; credits are family-pooled and may expire after a period
Exact credit costs per feature: not published (vary by feature)
access_route: Subscribe from gemini.google/subscriptions (or one.google.com) with a personal Google account in a supported country; manage seat, family members, and AI credits from the Google One dashboard.

claim_steps.step: Confirm the $19.99/mo figure on the official subscriptions page before checking out.
If eligible (18+, student status via SheerID), claim the 1-year student offer first — note it auto-renews at $19.99/mo after.
Check your country's availability and the third-party/Pixel Pass signup exclusions in the membership article.
After subscribing, review AI-credit purchases only if you actually hit a limit — pack prices appear at checkout, not in docs.

economics: Two ways to read the $19.99: as an AI plan it must beat Claude Pro/ChatGPT Plus on model access per dollar; as a bundle it competes with a storage plan plus several app subscriptions. The page's own extras (5 TB ≈ standalone paid storage tier, YouTube Premium Lite, Home Premium at '$10/mo value', $10/mo Cloud credits) are what make the sub-$20 sticker defensible.

Against the $0.80/task illustrative reference, $19.99 is parity at ~25 heavy AI tasks/mo — but unlike pure chat subs, part of the fee is storage and apps you may pay for separately anyway; assign that share before comparing AI-only.
Student free year makes marginal cost $0 for a year — the break-even logic only matters from month 13.
The unpublished annual price and credit-pack prices mean true cost comparison against annual-priced rivals (Claude $17/mo annual) cannot be done from official pages this pass.

evidence.point: The $19.99/mo price, '4x higher usage limits', the 5-hour/weekly limit wording, and 'No refunds for partial billing periods, except as required by law' are in the static text of the official Gemini subscriptions page fetched live.
Renewal (charge at cycle start, auto-renew), 30-day price-increase notice, seven-day failed-renewal grace, and family/billing mechanics come from Google One's official terms and help articles.
AI credits as the overage path (Pro/Ultra only, plan-manager purchase, family-pooled, expiring, modifiable costs) is documented officially; pack prices are absent from the doc itself.

150+ country availability, student 1-year offer terms (SheerID; renews at $19.99; no school accounts), and the 5 TB / 4x / feature lists are from the official AI-plans pages; third-party claims of a ~$49.99 10 TB tier were NOT confirmed on official pages and are not quoted.

faq.q: What does Google AI Pro cost as of the Sep 2026 snapshot?
faq.a: $19.99/month — verified in the static text of gemini.google/subscriptions on 2026-09-07. Annual billing is offered but no annual price appears on any official page fetched this pass.

faq.q: What usage limits does the plan actually state?
faq.a: '4x access to Gemini' vs non-subscribers, and the published mechanism: a limit that refreshes every 5 hours until you reach a weekly limit, applied per product. Exact prompt or generation counts are not published.

faq.q: Can I buy more usage when I hit the limit?
faq.a: Yes via Google's AI credits (plain-English: prepaid usage packs for Gemini, Flow, and Antigravity). Only the plan manager can buy them, they pool across the family, they may expire, and per-feature credit costs are unpublished and changeable by Google.

faq.q: What's in the bundle beyond chat?
faq.a: 5 TB storage (10 TB on some variants), Gemini in Gmail/Docs/Vids, Deep Research and 1M-context access, Flow/Flow Music, NotebookLM, Jules, Antigravity, Colab/AI Studio, Android Studio integration, Chrome auto-browse (US), YouTube Premium Lite, Google Home Premium Standard, and $10/mo Cloud credits — all per the official plans/help pages.

faq.q: How do cancellation and refunds work?
faq.a: Cancel anytime; benefits run to the end of the billing cycle, then storage reverts to 15 GB. Purchases are non-refundable in most regions (partial periods included); Apple-billed subscriptions refund through Apple; a seven-day grace period applies to failed renewals.
Live fetches of official Google pages 2026-09-07. Region availability and credit pricing shift often.
